findings.reason: parse_link_destination.mjs:52 now breaks with pos left on the backslash, where the old code did pos++ and broke at the space. link.mjs:62-76 then gets `\`, which is not whitespace, a title or `)`, so the link is rejected. I kept medium rather than X1's high because only the edge-case input of a backslash followed by a space is affected. No story.md exists, so I can't tie this to an AC.
findings.claim: An unbracketed destination ending in a literal backslash before a space (e.g. `[x](a\ )` or `[x](a\ "t")`) is no longer parsed as a link.
findings.evidence: The baseline ran `if (str.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 0x20) { pos++; continue }`, which kept the backslash in the destination and then broke at the space on the next iteration. The head runs `{ break }`, which leaves `pos` on the backslash. The caller then finds `\` where it expects whitespace, a title or `)`, so the link is rejected. The only fixture for this case (test/fixtures/markdown-it/commonmark_extras.txt:345, `[link](a\ b)` → not a link) gives the same result under both versions, so it doesn't exercise the behaviour that changed.
